claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children would you like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim for my daughter Alex. She's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to meet you.

Now, I have a few more questions about your circumstances regarding Alex:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you!

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, she lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Wonderful, thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for her.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

One final question:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, care, or residential accommodation provided by the local council?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, yes - she's been in hospital for a while now. She's been there for about 11 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. I hope Alex recovers well soon.

Since Alex has been in hospital for 11 weeks, this is important information. Child Benefit payments can be affected if a child is in hospital for more than 12 weeks.

I have a couple of follow-up questions:

**Are you regularly spending money on Alex while she's in hospital?** (For example, on things like clothes, toys, treats, or other items for her)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I still buy her clothes, magazines, and her favorite snacks and things when I visit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know, thank you.

**Is Alex in a hospital in the UK, or is she in hospital abroad?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: She's in a hospital here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all the information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- You live in the UK
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- Alex lives with you (when not in hospital)
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for her
- She has been in hospital for 11 weeks (under the 12-week limit)
- You are regularly spending money on her while she's in hospital
- The hospital is in the UK

Let me provide you with my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

✅ **You live in the UK** – This is a basic requirement for Child Benefit.

✅ **Alex is under 16** – At 8 years old, she meets the age criteria.

✅ **You are responsible for Alex** – She normally lives with you.

✅ **No one else is claiming** – Only one person can receive Child Benefit per child.

✅ **Hospital stay** – Although Alex has been in hospital for 11 weeks, this is still under the 12-week limit. Importantly, because you are regularly spending money on her (clothes, magazines, snacks, etc.) while she's in a UK hospital, you would continue to qualify for Child Benefit even if her stay exceeds 12 weeks.

**Important:** You should inform HMRC about Alex's hospital stay so they are aware of your circumstances. If her stay extends beyond 12 weeks, your regular spending on her will be taken into account to allow your Child Benefit to continue.

I hope Alex makes a speedy recovery! Is there anything else you'd like to know?
